title: Reject impossible dates in synthetic record-retention decisions
prompt:
Fix invalid-calendar acceptance in lib/ohworks-record-retention.ts. Its timestamp predicate at lines 163-164 checks only a Z suffix and Date.parse finiteness; lines 196-216 trust the resulting normalized date. I reproduced eligible_for_purge with retentionEndDate=2026-03-03T12:00:00.000Z for a synthetic QC_LOG created at nonexistent 2026-02-30T12:00:00Z, retentionPeriodMs=86400000, litigationHold=false, evaluated at 2026-03-04T12:00:00Z. lib/ohworks-demo-audit-integrity-view.ts:91 uses this evaluator for retention evidence displayed to users.

Strengthen the local UTC predicate to validate real calendar and clock fields, retaining Z timestamps with supported fractional seconds. Apply the same validation to creation, current, and manifest purge timestamps through their existing call sites. Return the existing typed creation-date-invalid, current-timestamp-invalid, or purge-timestamp-invalid errors as appropriate. Preserve missing-date errors, hold precedence for valid inputs, elapsed-time boundaries, and batch behavior. This is pure synthetic evaluation; do not delete records or add any persistence.

Add tests/ohworks/record-retention-calendar.test.ts for each invalid timestamp position, February 30, April 31, non-leap February 29, and valid leap-day controls. Verify an impossible purge timestamp is rejected even for an empty manifest batch. Run node --import tsx --test tests/ohworks/record-retention.test.ts tests/ohworks/record-retention-calendar.test.ts tests/ohworks/demo-audit-integrity-view.test.ts.

Planning verification reproduced the defect and passed existing evaluator and demo-view tests. Change only this source and new test. No credentials, deploys, sends, payments, migrations, auth, package.json, or workflow changes. work on the assigned branch you are on.
